div.h1: Intellectual Property: Filed Patent Applications and Open Source Publication
div.p: This page records, in one place, the two forms of intellectual property disclosure that exist side by side for the hams.com/hams_open project: USPTO provisional patent applications filed on specific inventions, and the separate, ongoing publication of the project's implementation code as open source. It exists so the relationship between the two is explicit and auditable, not something that has to be reconstructed from separate records.

Filer/inventor for all applications below: Bruce Perens (pro se, sole inventor). Full filing detail (attorney docket numbers, confirmation numbers, Patent Center submission numbers, receipt timestamps, payment records) is maintained in the project's internal filing record (docs/proposals/patent_disclosures/filed_applications/USPTO_FILING_RECORD.md); this page lists only the USPTO-assigned application serial numbers, for quick reference.

div.p: All 43 applications above are Utility - Provisional Applications under 35 U.S.C. § 111(b), filed under USPTO Customer Number 244826, Micro Entity status. A provisional application is not examined and does not itself issue as a patent; each establishes a priority date for a future non-provisional filing within the following 12 months.

Regulator AI Global, Inc. (https://regulator-ai.com/) is reported to have filed additional patents in a related space. As of this writing no specific application, serial, or publication number is known, and it has not been confirmed whether these have actually been submitted to the USPTO or any other patent office. Bruce Perens is reported as a co-inventor on these with Regulator AI Global, Inc., and these patents are intended to be licensed to hams.com. This entry is a placeholder for awareness/tracking purposes only and should be updated with specific numbers once/if they become available.
Independent of the patent filings above, the project's implementation code is published as open source on GitHub under the BrucePerens account:

Both repositories are public as of this writing. Licensing is not uniform across every file (see hams_open/LICENSING.md for the authoritative, file-by-file survey), but the overwhelming majority of the codebase — every Odoo addon module (models, controllers, views) in both repositories — is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later. Known, deliberate exceptions: the Rust daemons/ham_digital_modes/ decoder daemon is LGPL-3.0-or-later, and the mypy Odoo-type-stub tooling under hams_shared/tools/ is GPL-3.0-or-later. hams_shared is tracked as its own independent git submodule of hams_open, with its own commit history, but its files carry the same per-file license-header convention described above.
